title: Portable Add-On in the Medicaid Rate for Home Oxygen Therapy — Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility
content:
**Memo.** In an Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility crossover, the portable add-on that enters the Medicaid monthly rate is reckoned by the patient's prescribed flow and use, read from the patient's Home Oxygen Therapy record (prescribed flow and usage pattern) and the class's fee-schedule figures (the stationary fee, the portable add-on and the high-flow threshold and uplift).

| Situation | Portable add-on entering the rate |
|---|---|
| Prescribed flow above the class's high-flow threshold (4 liters per minute in every class), on a class furnishing portable equipment, for a patient whose usage pattern is not sleep only | only the part by which the stationary fee plus the portable add-on exceeds the stationary fee raised by the class's high-flow uplift (50 percent in every class), never below zero — so that the higher of the two amounts applies |
| Usage pattern sleep only | no portable add-on |
| Any other case | the full portable add-on |

## Worked figures (hypothetical class fees: stationary 180.00, portable add-on 30.00)

| Case | Working | Add-on entering the rate |
|---|---|---|
| Flow 5, continuous use | 180.00 plus 30.00 is 210.00; the stationary fee raised by 50 percent is 270.00; 210.00 less 270.00 is below zero | 0.00 |
| Flow 3, exertion and sleep | flow not above 4 | 30.00 |
| Flow 5, sleep only | sleep only | 0.00 |
| Flow 5, exertion only, class with no portable equipment | not a portable class | the full add-on of that class, 0.00 |

Hypothetical with a large add-on: stationary 100.00, add-on 70.00, flow 5, continuous: 170.00 less 150.00 is 20.00, so 20.00 enters the rate.
